headline: ASX 200 rose 1% today as local ETFs held firm, but last night's NASDAQ selloff (-2.15%) weighed on US holdings — oil surging past $100 on Iran tensions is the big story to watch.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Strong bounce today on the ASX — AI sentiment got a lift locally even as US tech slipped overnight. The ETF tracks AI-exposed companies globally, so local buying interest and a solid ASX session pushed it up. Still down about 10% overall from your entry price, but today's move is encouraging.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Slipped last night alongside the broader NASDAQ selloff. No specific Take-Two news driving the move — it's caught in the general tech/growth stock downdraft as markets get nervous ahead of US earnings season. Long-term thesis around Grand Theft Auto VI release is unchanged.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet fell last night despite some positive analyst notes — Evercore actually raised estimates on potential TPU (Google's AI chip) hardware sales. The drop looks like broad tech selling rather than company-specific bad news. The market is rotating cautiously ahead of earnings.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dipped last night with the broader NASDAQ. Markets are tempering expectations ahead of Q1 earnings — analysts flagging a $25B cost problem related to AI infrastructure spending. Last quarter's massive post-earnings rally is unlikely to repeat, per Yahoo Finance.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Solid session on the ASX today, riding the broader market's 1% gain. VDHG holds a diversified mix of global shares, so the local tailwind helped. Nothing specific driving it — just a good day for the market overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Up today on the ASX even though US markets fell last night — this is an ASX-listed ETF so it trades in AUD during local hours and had a good session. The slight AUD strength may have trimmed some of the overnight US market weakness when repriced today.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: Quiet but positive session — moved with the broader ASX 200 which gained 1% today. DHHF is a set-and-forget diversified growth ETF, so a steady up day is exactly what you want.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Modest gain today. Emerging markets have been under pressure from oil price spikes (many EM economies are oil importers), so the small move is respectable in that environment.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Essentially flat today despite a major positive announcement — PLS approved a large lithium expansion at Pilgangoora and reported 31% growth in contained lithium ore reserves. The lack of a bigger price reaction likely reflects ongoing headwinds: lithium prices dropped 14% on news of an EU-China hybrid car deal that reduces long-term demand forecasts. It's a tug of war between company-specific good news and a difficult market backdrop.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings coming — manage expectations
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports Q1 results soon (US time). Analysts are warning the massive post-earnings rally from last quarter won't repeat this time. There's a $25B AI infrastructure cost problem flagged by Seeking Alpha, and the stock is already priced at 27.5x earnings. Last night it dipped nearly 2%. For a long-term holder, sit tight — but be ready for short-term volatility around the print.

watch_today.title: PLS: Big reserves upgrade, but lithium headwinds persist
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals today announced a 31% jump in contained lithium ore reserves at Pilgangoora AND approved a major expansion. That's genuinely good long-term news. BUT lithium prices just fell 14% on an EU-China hybrid car deal that dents demand expectations. PLS is already down ~56% from your cost base. The long-term case depends on lithium demand recovering — that story is intact but taking longer than hoped. Hold and wait.

watch_today.title: GXAI bounced 3% today — AI ETF showing some life
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF had a strong session on the ASX today, up 3.15%. Still down about 10% overall from your entry, but today's move shows the AI theme isn't dead. With Anthropic pushing for AI regulation (which could entrench big players) and NVIDIA launching new AI PCs, the sector has ongoing catalysts. Long-term hold — no need to act.

watch_today.title: Oil above $100 — watch for inflation ripple effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil touched $110 a barrel overnight on Iran war fears before pulling back to around $101 — still up 3.5% for the session. If oil stays elevated, it feeds back into global inflation, which could push central banks (including the RBA) to keep rates higher for longer. That's a headwind for growth stocks and property. Something to watch this week.

watch_today.title: NASDAQ down 2.15% last night — your US holdings took a hit
watch_today.detail: Last night's NASDAQ selloff dragged GOOG (-2.32%), MSFT (-1.93%), and TTWO (-1.96%) lower. It was broad tech selling ahead of US earnings season rather than anything specific to these companies. The long-term thesis for all three is intact — a single down night is noise for a buy-and-hold investor. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Analyst upgrades but stock still fell — good sign for long term
watch_today.detail: Despite Alphabet dropping 2.3% last night, Evercore actually raised its estimates on the potential for Google to sell its TPU AI chips externally — a new revenue stream that could significantly grow the cloud business. The drop was market-wide selling, not stock-specific bad news. Long-term holders should feel comfortable staying put.

world.summary: The Iran conflict is rattling oil markets and shipping lanes, US midterm election integrity is under serious pressure from the Trump administration, and 'Dr Doom' economist Nouriel Roubini has fresh warnings for global markets.

stories.title: Iran war sends oil above $100 — ships in Strait of Hormuz under attack
stories.why_it_matters: Oil briefly hit $110 a barrel overnight — its highest since May — as the conflict involving Iran continues to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil chokepoint. Maritime monitors are warning of 'indiscriminate attacks' on ships in the strait. Even though prices pulled back a little to around $101, that's still a 3.5% jump in one session. Higher oil means higher petrol prices for everyday Australians and adds to global inflation pressure, making interest rate cuts less likely.

stories.title: Trump administration threatens California election officials ahead of midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is threatening to prosecute local California election workers if non-citizens are found to have voted in next month's US midterm elections. Critics — including the Campaign Legal Center — say the administration is laying groundwork to challenge or undermine election results. The New York Times reports that 2020 election conspiracy theories are actively shaping how the federal government is preparing for these midterms. This is a significant escalation in US political tensions with real implications for democratic stability in America's largest state.

stories.title: Iran president labels Middle East conflict 'ecocide'
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's president has publicly described the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as 'ecocide' — meaning large-scale, deliberate destruction of the natural environment. The statement escalates the diplomatic rhetoric and signals Iran isn't backing down. With oil shipping routes already under attack and prices spiking, any further escalation could push oil even higher and deepen instability across the region. Everyday Australians feel this through petrol prices and broader cost-of-living pressure.

stories.title: 'Dr Doom' Nouriel Roubini has fresh forecasts — and they're not pretty
stories.why_it_matters: Nouriel Roubini — the economist who famously predicted the 2008 global financial crisis — has published fresh forecasts. While the article doesn't detail his full predictions, Roubini has consistently warned about stagflation (slow growth plus high inflation), debt crises, and geopolitical shocks. With oil prices spiking and US political instability rising, his warnings are getting fresh attention from investors globally. Worth being aware of if you're thinking about long-term portfolio risk.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a good day, closing up 1% to 8,806. Last night, the US story was all about a big NASDAQ selloff — tech got hammered down 2.15% and the S&P 500 dropped 1.09%. Oil is the headline mover, jumping 3.5% to over $101 a barrel on Iran conflict fears. Gold crept up slightly and the Aussie dollar edged higher to nearly 69.5 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid local session — ASX closed up 1% today.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session: fell 1.09% as markets got nervous ahead of US earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night: tech sold off hard, down 2.15%. Growth stocks took the brunt.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big spike — oil hit $110 briefly on Iran/Strait of Hormuz fears before settling around $101.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Nudged higher — investors adding a little safe-haven exposure amid geopolitical tension.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar edged up — RBA rate hike bets eased slightly, but AUD still holding near 69.5c.

politics.summary: Australia's unemployment rate has risen to 4.7%, the RBA governor's $1.2M pay packet is drawing scrutiny as staff fight wage cuts, and a credit squeeze could hit property prices. Plus, the government has begun overhauling heritage laws after the McPhillamys mine ruling.

stories.title: Unemployment hits 4.7% — the RBA got what it wished for
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's unemployment rate has climbed to 4.7%, which is actually something the Reserve Bank of Australia has been aiming for — higher unemployment means less wage pressure and less inflation. For everyday Aussies, this means more people are out of work, and it also signals the economy is slowing down. The silver lining is that this reduces the chance of further RBA interest rate hikes, which is good for mortgage holders.

stories.title: RBA governor paid $1.2M while workers fight real wage cuts
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA governor is being paid $1.2 million a year while RBA staff are in a dispute over wages they say are failing to keep up with inflation — effectively a real pay cut. The story puts the spotlight on the disconnect between executive pay at Australia's central bank and the cost-of-living pressures hitting its own workforce. It's a politically awkward moment for the RBA as it lectures the country about wage restraint.

stories.title: Credit squeeze could deliver fresh blow to property prices
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is reporting that tighter lending conditions — a 'credit squeeze' — could put further downward pressure on Australian property prices. With unemployment rising and banks becoming more cautious about who they lend to, fewer people can borrow as much as before. That reduces buyer demand and can push prices down. For property owners or anyone thinking of buying, this is worth watching closely over the coming months.

stories.title: Heritage laws overhaul begins after McPhillamys mine ruling
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has begun overhauling Australia's heritage laws in the wake of the McPhillamys gold mine ruling, where heritage protections blocked a major mining project in NSW. The changes are aimed at creating clearer rules about when cultural heritage claims can halt or delay resource projects. This matters for mining investors — it could affect approvals for projects involving PLS and other resource companies down the track.

ai.summary: AI regulation is dominating the headlines this week, with Anthropic — the company behind the Claude AI assistant — actively lobbying US lawmakers for new laws. Meanwhile, NVIDIA launched new AI-powered PCs and a new malware is targeting AI chatbot users.

stories.title: Anthropic takes AI regulation bill directly to US lawmakers
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the startup behind the Claude AI chatbot and one of the most influential AI companies in the world — is actively circulating a draft AI regulation bill among US lawmakers. The company's co-founder is calling for 'common sense standards' for the most powerful AI systems (known as 'frontier AI'). This is significant because Anthropic is essentially asking to be regulated, which would likely set rules that smaller competitors struggle to meet — potentially locking in the big players. Expect this to shape US AI policy over the next year.

stories.title: NVIDIA launches RTX Spark AI PCs — available now
stories.why_it_matters: NVIDIA has launched its RTX Spark range of AI-focused Windows PCs, available from today. These are consumer PCs with dedicated AI processing chips built in — designed to run AI tasks (like local chatbots, image generation, and coding assistants) directly on your own machine rather than in the cloud. It's a meaningful step toward AI becoming part of everyday computing, not just something that lives on the internet. Good news for NVIDIA's revenue and for your GXAI ETF which holds AI-chip-exposed companies.

stories.title: New 'Aoki' malware is stealing login details for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
stories.why_it_matters: A new piece of malware called 'Aoki' has been discovered that specifically targets users of major AI chatbots — including ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, and Gemini — to steal their login credentials. If you use any of these AI tools, it's worth making sure you have two-factor authentication turned on and that you're not clicking on dodgy links or downloading software from unverified sources. As AI tools become more central to work and daily life, they're becoming more attractive targets for hackers.

stories.title: Jais 3 launches — powerful Arabic-language AI with 375 billion parameters
stories.why_it_matters: A new family of Arabic-language AI models called Jais 3 has launched, with the largest model containing 375 billion parameters — making it one of the biggest AI models ever built for a non-English language. This is part of a broader global push to build AI that works well in languages beyond English, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa. It signals that AI development is genuinely going global, not just staying in Silicon Valley.

sport.summary: It's Rugby League World Cup time — Tonga stunned England overnight for a historic win, Samoa had a solid opener, and there's a big name NRL suspension saga brewing. Plus some AFL news including a shock retirement and a drug testing overhaul.

stories.title: Tonga stun England in historic Rugby League World Cup win
stories.why_it_matters: Tonga pulled off a massive upset in the Rugby League World Cup, beating England in what NRL.com is calling a 'historic win' — a huge statement from the Pacific nation on the international stage. England were considered heavy favourites. It's the kind of result that reshapes the entire tournament picture and announces Tonga as genuine title contenders.

stories.title: Samoa make strong start — four tries to Fa'alogo in World Cup opener
stories.why_it_matters: Samoa opened their Rugby League World Cup campaign strongly, with one player — Fa'alogo — scoring four tries in the game. Samoa have been one of the most entertaining sides in international rugby league and look to have carried that form into the tournament. With Tonga also winning big, Pacific teams could dominate this World Cup.

stories.title: Josh Addo-Carr faces monster ban — even if Eels grant him a lifeline
stories.why_it_matters: Josh Addo-Carr, the Parramatta Eels flyer, is staring down a 'monster ban' according to Fox Sports — and critically, even if the Eels give him a contract lifeline, the suspension looms large. The specifics of what he's done aren't detailed in the headline, but the severity suggests it could sideline him for a significant chunk of next season. A big development for Eels fans and NRL finals planning.

stories.title: AFL player announces shock retirement at age 28
stories.why_it_matters: A three-club AFL player has announced immediate retirement at just 28 years old — well short of the typical career endpoint. The AFL world has paid tribute, suggesting the player was well-respected. Early retirements at 28 are rare and often come down to physical or mental health reasons. The name isn't in the article title, but the AFL community's reaction suggests it's a meaningful loss for the game.

stories.title: NRL wins first round in 'Chiefs' name trademark battle
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has won the first legal skirmish in a trademark dispute over the 'Chiefs' name — a battle that's heading to court. This is about whether an NRL team can use that name given it's also used by the Super Rugby Chiefs franchise. The parties are preparing to 'duke it out' in court, which could have implications for team branding and commercial rights across rugby codes in Australia and New Zealand.
